- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase baseline or allow slight upward bias.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >80), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; apply a “cool-down” rule: cap forecast at +5–10% above peak for 3–5 days.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model often lags; adjust forecast to align with sentiment change within 2–3 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >85 for 3+ consecutive days, reduce slope or add downward bias.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.33/1.00), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast with 3-day moving average or reduce volatility coefficient.
